settings.description: The value the Anthropic adapter sends in the anthropic-version header. Gateways that speak the Messages API, such as Ollama and LiteLLM, expect this one.

How many times the Anthropic adapter sends a call again when it failed before any of the reply arrived and the failure may pass: a rate limit, a busy provider, or an endpoint that could not be reached. Zero means never.
How long the Anthropic adapter waits before its first retry. Each later wait is twice the one before.
The longest the Anthropic adapter waits before a retry. When the provider asks for a longer wait, the call fails at once so another model can be tried.
How long an endpoint that speaks the Anthropic Messages API may take to begin its answer. A local model that has to be loaded first needs the time. Zero means no limit.
How long a reply from the Anthropic adapter's endpoint may send nothing before the call is given up. Zero means no limit.
Whether the Anthropic adapter marks the end of the system blocks and of the last message so the provider can cache what comes before.

The provider model names, separated by commas, that are asked for thinking as a token budget. A name ending in * matches by its start. Every other model is asked for adaptive thinking, where the model decides how much to think.
How many characters the fake provider sends in each piece of a streamed reply. Zero sends each block in one piece.
How long the fake provider waits before each piece of a streamed reply, so a chat in the test tenant streams at a speed a person can watch. Tests use no wait.
The most models one person's registry may hold. Adding one more is refused.
